claims.text: Baseline NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Baseline NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
Baseline NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
The irradiation resistance of baseline NbMoTaW has not been experimentally verified.
Substituting approximately 5 at% vanadium for an unspecified base element and applying thermomechanical processing will improve room-temperature ductility.
The vanadium addition and thermomechanical processing will improve irradiation tolerance.
The modified alloy will retain the high-temperature strength of untreated NbMoTaW up to 1600 °C.
The modified alloy will retain a BCC matrix and BCC phase stability.
Hot working and controlled annealing will refine the grain structure and modify grain-boundary chemistry.
The processing will produce grain boundaries locally enriched in vanadium.
The processing may produce nanoscale precipitates that act as irradiation-defect sinks.
Vanadium enrichment and possible precipitates will modify local lattice parameters and create sites for defect annihilation.
Vanadium lowers the local Peierls barrier in NbMoTaW.
A lower Peierls barrier and altered lattice parameters will increase dislocation mobility and thereby enhance room-temperature ductility.
Engineered grain boundaries will absorb vacancies, interstitials, and helium atoms during irradiation.
Absorption of irradiation defects at engineered grain boundaries will mitigate helium bubbles, blistering, and potential amorphization.
The modified alloy will increase room-temperature strain to failure by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
The modified alloy will exhibit fewer helium bubbles and less blistering than untreated NbMoTaW under approximately 500 keV helium implantation.
Secondary-phase formation or undesirable grain-boundary segregation at the selected vanadium concentration could impair high-temperature performance or BCC stability.
